newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile president's popularity slips a bit - poll.
newsitem.headline: Chile president's popularity slips a bit - poll.

text.p: President Eduardo Frei's popularity has fallen slightly over the last year, with 45.4 percent of Chileans approving his conduct, down from 48.2 percent in March 1996, a poll released on Friday said.
"The figure continues being quite high, although significantly lower than the 53-54 percent seen in the first 18 months of his term," the report from agency Adimark said.
The poll was carried out last month, halfway through Frei's six-year presidential term.
Former President Patricio Aylwin received a 58 percent approval rating when he had been in power for three years in March 1993.
The poll also indicated a rise in dissatisfaction with the government. Now 30.2 percent of Chileans disapprove of the government's performance, up from 25 percent a year ago.
The government won most praise for its handling of international relations, but the survey showed a fall in approval of its anti-terrorist policies after a spectacular guerrilla jailbreak last year.
"Without doubt this (fall) is related to the escape of the terrorists last December which has still not been solved," said the report.

The poll showed a sharp rise in the popularity of socialist leader and Public Works Minister Ricardo Lagos who is widely tipped as the ruling centre-left coalition's candidate in the next presidential elections in 1999.
Lagos was mentioned as the "most important" political figure in the country by 50 percent of Chileans polled, up 10 percent from March 1996.
Santiago mayor Joaquin Lavin, who won an overwhelming victory in municipal elections last year, emerged as the most popular leader in the right-wing opposition, it said.
The poll surveyed 1,545 people over 18 years old. It has a margin of error of 3.1 percent.
